intent_en: Analyze the share of adults with a great deal of confidence in police officers across racial and ethnic groups, and determine how the groups compare.
narration_support: White adults are much more likely than black or Hispanic adults to say that they have a great deal of confidence in the police.
chart_support: Horizontal bar chart comparing the percentage of adults with a great deal of confidence in police officers by race and ethnicity, showing White adults with the highest proportion and Black adults with the lowest.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly discusses race as a fault line for police confidence and states White adults are more likely to have confidence, which aligns with the chart showing White adults at 32% versus lower percentages for other groups. narrative_goal: To illustrate the racial and ethnic disparities in public confidence in police officers, demonstrating that White adults express significantly higher confidence than Black, Hispanic, and Asian adults.
